excerpt: Spenmo was a Singapore spend management startup for bill payments, corporate cards and reimbursements. Its website says it ceased operations on 14 August 2025. History and alternatives.
content:
Spenmo was a Singapore company that sold spend management software to small and mid-sized businesses in Southeast Asia. Its product, as still described on its website, covered bill payments with document scanning and approval workflows, physical and virtual Visa corporate debit cards, employee reimbursements with multi-level approvals, and integrations with accounting tools such as Xero, NetSuite and QuickBooks. Payments and cards were provided through partners licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore; the site notes that Spenmo itself was not licensed under the Payment Services Act.

Spenmo has shut down. A notice on spenmo.com says the company ceased business operations on 14 August 2025 at 23:59:59 Singapore time, that customer dashboard access was permanently disabled, and that support for existing tickets ended on 21 August 2025.

The years before the closure were turbulent. DealStreetAsia reported in early 2022 that Spenmo raised $85.35 million in a Series B led by Tiger Global. In October 2023 DealStreetAsia reported that it was shutting down its services in the Philippines, one of its main markets. Fintech News Singapore reported in June 2025 that the company had rebranded as Summit in July 2024, repositioning around accounts-payable automation, after co-founder Mohandass Kalaichelvan stepped down as CEO and his successor, Justin Choi, left after about a month. The same report said Summit laid off 24 of its 64 employees across Singapore, Indonesia and India, under CEO Jo-Ann Chung.

There is no Spenmo product to buy or price today. Businesses that relied on it will need another spend management or accounts-payable tool; some options are listed below.

This page is research, not a review. We never used Spenmo; facts come from its website and the reporting under Sources.
